column1: # The 34-arm two-task WEIGHT quant ladder. One arm per line, in execution order.
# Availability of every target and draft below was verified against the
# HuggingFace file listings on 2026-08-16. Nothing here is assumed to exist.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   order     execution order
#   label     unique arm id; becomes the results filename stem
#   model     model key; all arms sharing one key form one ladder
#   train     base | qat
#   width     q1 | q2 | q4 | q6 | q8 | bf16
#   target    llama-server -hf argument
#   draft     llama-server -hfd argument, or "-" for no speculation
#   est_gib   estimated on-disk size, for ordering and the footprint guard only.
#             NOT a measurement. The real resident size is recorded per arm.
# The ladder rungs are non-QAT because the QAT repositories publish only Q4
# (and Q2 for E2B/E4B). QAT therefore appears as an extra arm at those widths
# rather than as a rung. See moe-ladder-plan-2026-08-16.md.
# Within a model: base Q4 first (the slow-arm rule needs it as the baseline),
# its QAT counterpart second (adjacent in time on the same card), then the
# cheap low rungs, then Q6 and Q8 which are the arms at risk of spilling.
# BF16 for LFM2.5-2.6B was added on 2026-08-16 after that ladder completed and
# showed a monotonic DECLINE with width: Q8 minus Q4 came out -0.0327 with a
# 95% range of [-0.0592, -0.0063], clearing zero, while throughput fell 32%.
# BF16 is the unquantised reference and therefore the sharpest test of that
# result: if accuracy keeps falling at full precision then quantisation is not
# what is degrading it, and the cause lies elsewhere. At ~5.2 GiB it is dense
# and fully card-resident, so it costs one arm and confounds nothing.
# The KV cache is f16 on EVERY arm, which is llama.cpp's default, and ctk/ctv
# are held constant rather than removed so the configuration stays provable per
# arm rather than implied by absence.
# A KV precision sweep ran here on 2026-08-16/17 and has been REMOVED. Cache
# precision is a separate subject with its own scaling behaviour -- KV grows
# with context x layers x heads while weights do not -- so it belongs to its own
# study rather than as a second axis inside a weight ladder. The three arms that
# completed are recorded in articles/kv-cache-precision/, which also states why
# that measurement is not yet publishable: it fixes context at 8192, which is
# the one variable the subject is about.
# Their extraction results are banked and nothing is lost by dropping them here.
# Removing them also drops the ~5 hours of synthesis still queued against them
# and the unrun q4_0/q4_0 arm.
order
